thread.title: Why Apple (AAPL) Stock Can Withstand A Chinese Trade War

author: Richard Saintvilus
title: Why Apple (AAPL) Stock Can Withstand A Chinese Trade War
text:
Shutterstock photo
The likelihood of a trade war with China has taken a significant toll on a number of tech stocks, as evidenced by the recent declines in the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite Index.
Eager to fix what is perceived as unfair trade practices from China, the Trump administration said it would impose a 25% tariff on more than 1,300 imported goods Chinese goods, totaling $50 billion worth of Chinese products that will feel the effect of the new tariffs annually.
As President Trump works to make good on his campaign promise to forge a better trade deals, investors grapple with the potential adverse effects retaliatory tariffs can have on corporate bottom lines, particularly from companies that derive sizable positions of their sales from the world’s most populous country.
Apple ( AAPL ), which has made China its second-largest market, is high on the list of companies with the most at stake . Out of the $229 billion in sales reported for fiscal 2017, about $45 billion, or roughly 20% came from China, according to financial researcher FactSet. That $45 billion figure ranks the highest among all S&P 500 companies. Chipmakers Intel ( INTC ) and Qualcomm ( QCOM ) came in second and third, respectively with sales of $14.7 billion and $14.5 billion, respectively.
However, from a percentage perspective, the story changes. That 20% of Apple’s sales comes from China is not that significant, compared to Qualcomm’s 65% and Intel’s 23%. While 20% is high compared to FAANG peers Facebook ( FB ), Amazon ( AMZN ), Netflix ( NFLX ) and Google ( GOOG , GOOGL ), that’s partly because these are mostly internet or service-based companies, while Apple not only manufactures hardware in China, it also sells goods there.
In the most recent quarter, Apple's revenue from China grew 11% year over year to $18 billion, topping analysts forecast for a 9% increase. But a perceived risk of a trade war with China has spooked investors to take profits prior to upcoming quarter. Not only Apple stock fallen into correction territory, the risk from China has prompted some analysts to lower their price targets and in some cases, reduce iPhone sales estimates. But that seems highly premature at this point.
While a trade war, assuming one ensues, could result in higher manufacturing costs for Apple, and thus eat at its profit margins, the impact would be minimal , according to Gene Munster, analysts at Loup Ventures. And that's because the bulk of Apple’s products are manufactured outside of the United States. What’s more, the tariffs — as it stands — would impact raw materials like aluminum and steel, meaning Apple would see little impact to its products, if any.
Investors are nonetheless jittery, given all of the political posturing. It’s for this reason that since reaching a high of $183.50 on March 13, Apple shares have fallen as much as 10%. And now would be a good time to buy. The stock is priced at just 15 times fiscal 2018 estimates of $11.44 per share, which is three points lower than the S&P 500 index. When adjusting out the cash, Apple’s P/E drops to single digits, making it one of the best bargains on the market.
